description.value: Established in 1925 and named after the Sullivan Mine that anchored Kimberley's economy for over a century, The Sullivan Pub (locally 'The Sully') is one of the town's most storied gathering spots. It serves a full pub menu of hearty classics and creative dishes alongside a wide selection of local and craft beers. Regular live music nights, karaoke, and music bingo make it a lively community hub, and an adjacent drive-through liquor store adds convenience for stocking up.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website at sullivanpub.com is fully accessible and confirms the pub's address (400 Ross St, Kimberley BC), phone (250-427-5516), and active operation with upcoming 2026 events. Takeout is explicitly described on both the homepage and menu page ('All Take-out orders to be picked at the Sully Liquor Store Drive Thru next door to the pub'). No mention of bike parking, water refill, washrooms, or most amenities appears on the website; OSM tags internet_access=wlan but the website does not corroborate this, so it is left null per instructions.
concerns: OSM addr:housenumber tag is incorrectly set to '400 Ross St' (a full street address) rather than just '400'; this causes the OSM address field to read '400 Ross St Ross Street, V1A 2C6' with the street name duplicated. Website confirms the correct address as 400 Ross St, Kimberley BC.
OSM tags internet_access=wlan but the website makes no mention of Wi-Fi; left null pending confirmation.
Dine-in is restricted to patrons 19+ per BC liquor regulations; this is not a concern for adult touring cyclists but worth noting.
The adjacent Sully Liquor Store has a separate phone number (250-427-3030) listed on the /liquor-store subpage, distinct from the pub's number.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: The Sullivan is a well-established, active pub and legitimate food-and-drink stop for touring cyclists in Kimberley, but none of the three required WWC criteria (bike parking/visibility, water refill, washrooms) could be confirmed from the website. A quick on-the-ground check or staff inquiry would likely resolve all three.
